question: What is the chemical composition of washing soda?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Na2CO3.10H2O**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The chemical formula for washing soda is **Na2CO3.10H2O**, which stands for sodium carbonate decahydrate.
 
• Washing soda is a **water-soluble sodium salt** of carbonic acid.
 
• It is commonly used in **laundry detergents** as a water softener.
 
• Washing soda is also used in the **manufacture of glass, paper, rayon, soaps, and detergents**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sodium Carbonate (Na2CO3)**

 
 
• It is a white, odorless powder that is hygroscopic in nature.
 
• It can be synthetically produced from sodium chloride (common salt) and limestone through the Solvay process.
 
• Sodium carbonate is also known as soda ash or soda crystals.
 
• It is used in water treatment to raise pH levels.
 
 
 
• **Decahydrate (10H2O)**
 
 
• Decahydrate means that each molecule of sodium carbonate is associated with ten molecules of water.
 
• It is important for the crystalline structure and properties of washing soda.
 
 
 
• **Hydration Process**
 
 
• When sodium carbonate is exposed to water, it absorbs water molecules and forms washing soda.
 
• This process is known as hydration.
 
 
 
• **Water Softening**
 
 
• Washing soda helps to soften water by removing calcium and magnesium ions.
 
• This improves the effectiveness of soaps and detergents in cleaning.
